trust_decision.summary: In HTTP transport mode a caller is trusted only if it presents its own NetLicensing API key; at the pinned commit a request with no key is forwarded unchanged (server.py:2039), so the shared upstream client authenticates with the server-side NETLICENSING_API_KEY environment default (client.py:29-31, client.py:61-67) instead of rejecting the caller.

landing_point.why: The advisory names ApiKeyMiddleware and HTTP mode; this class, defined inside main(), is the only authentication code in the tree and its final fallthrough is the reported behaviour.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP transport only: `netlicensing-mcp http` / MCP_TRANSPORT=http serves the streamable-HTTP endpoint /mcp over uvicorn (server.py:2014-2053)
fix_sites.module_kind: ASGI middleware defined inside the CLI entry-point function

fix_sites.entry_point: the uvicorn runner that builds mcp.streamable_http_app() and attaches the middleware to it

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site and no O8 route exists; the nearest argument a solver could make is that stdio mode has no remote caller so its env-key/demo:demo fallback is by design, and that the documented ?apikey= path is a client key source rather than an unauthenticated route.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The /health custom route must stay reachable with no key (ALB / App Runner / ECS liveness probes), and stdio mode plus the demo:demo sandbox fallback must keep working when no key exists at all; a blanket 401 or a guard placed in client._headers() breaks one of them.

?apikey= query parameter (accepted before the fix, dropped by it)
header key takes precedence over Bearer

O7_producer.where: src/netlicensing_mcp/client.py:29-31 (ContextVar default read from NETLICENSING_API_KEY at import), consumed at src/netlicensing_mcp/client.py:61-67

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a module-level ASGI `app` exported for `uvicorn netlicensing_mcp.server:app` that is built from mcp.streamable_http_app() without the middleware
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project already wraps the FastMCP app in uvicorn here and the AWS docs advertise a generic streamable-HTTP client, so exporting `app` for other container platforms is a natural next edit.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second @mcp.custom_route (e.g. /version or /status) that makes a cheap NetLicensing call with the server-side key
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The /health custom route already demonstrates the pattern, and a status route that validates credentials against the upstream API is an obvious neighbour a maintainer could add.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a legacy SSE transport branch (mcp.run(transport='sse') or mcp.sse_app()) that never passes through the streamable-HTTP middleware
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: FastMCP supports several transports and the CLI already takes a transport argument, so adding an SSE mode beside http/stdio is plausible.

O9_family: missing authentication for a critical function (CWE-306): the HTTP transport forwards keyless requests and then acts upstream with the server-side API key
